item.title: Home Assistant Custom Integration
item.description:
Recommended for Home Assistant Users

The hydroqc-ha custom integration is the recommended way to integrate Hydro-Québec with Home Assistant. It provides a native integration built directly into Home Assistant.

Why choose hydroqc-ha?

  • Native integration: Runs as a Home Assistant custom component
  • Easy configuration: Setup entirely through the Home Assistant interface
  • Full feature support: Consumption, billing, winter credits and dynamic pricing
  • Multiple contracts: One device per Hydro-Québec contract
  • Diagnostic entities: Optional entities for troubleshooting and advanced automations

Installation

Via HACS (Recommended)

Prerequisites

Make sure HACS is installed on your Home Assistant instance. If not:

item.title: Translation System
item.description:
Overview

The HydroQC integration uses Home Assistant’s built-in translation system to display sensor and entity names in your preferred language. The integration supports English, French, and Spanish.

How Translation Works

Home Assistant determines which language to display based on a specific priority order:

  1. System Language (highest priority)
  2. User Profile Language (fallback)
  3. Default Language (English) (final fallback)

This means that entity names will appear in the language configured for your entire Home Assistant system, not necessarily the language set in your individual user profile.

item.title: Energy Dashboard
item.description:
Hourly Consumption in Energy Dashboard

Disable Consumption Sync

If you don’t need consumption tracking or use another integration for this, you can disable consumption sync during initial setup or in the integration options. This prevents hourly consumption statistics from being imported and disables the history sync service.

Hourly consumption from Hydro-Québec is not live. The hourly consumption will sync automatically when it is available from Hydro-Québec. On the website you can only see the hourly consumption from the previous day. There is always a delay of a few hours before HQ publishes the information.

item.title: Price tracking
item.description:
Price tracking

There is no accurate way to track the rate price currently since all the sensors available track data from the day before.

If you don’t care about accuracy, you can also add the Bill Total to Date sensor under the option “Use an entity tracking the total costs”. This will display rate data, but it will calculate the price from yesterday with the consumption of the current day.

item.title: Other sensors
item.description:
Overview

Other manual configurations can be added to your system to display additional information related to Hydro-Québec.

The Domo-Québec Github project contains Hydro-Québec specific configurations

item.title: Sensors
item.description:
Overview

The integration defines 41 sensors and 18 binary sensors. Only the entities that apply to the configured rate are created for a contract. Entity names are translated by Home Assistant (English, French and Spanish); the names below are the English ones.

Entities marked Diagnostic are shown in the Diagnostic section of the device and are excluded from default dashboards. Some diagnostic entities are also disabled by default; enable them in the entity settings if needed.

item.title: Blueprint for Winter Credits
item.description:
Home-Assistant Blueprint

A Home-Assistant Blueprint with the options to carry out the automations described in this section is available here and can be installed directly with this button:

Blueprint Architecture

The Winter Credits blueprint uses a hybrid approach combining time-based triggers and calendar triggers:

Time-Based Triggers

Daily winter schedule (December 1 - March 31):

  • 01:00 : Morning anchor start
  • 04:00 : Morning anchor end
  • 06:00 : Morning peak start
  • 10:00 : Morning peak end
  • 12:00 : Evening anchor start
  • 14:00 : Evening anchor end
  • 16:00 : Evening peak start
  • 20:00 : Evening peak end

These time-based triggers ensure your automations fire at each anchor and peak period, whether critical or regular.

item.title: Optimization logics
item.description:
The following information is derived from the formulas from this “Régie de l’énergie” filing:

http://publicsde.regie-energie.qc.ca/projets/469/DocPrj/R-4057-2018-B-0062-DDR-RepDDR-2018_10_26.pdf#page=127

Overview

The winter credit program implement a set of calculations to estimate the real amount of energy you saved during a critical peak event. In short, they use the consumption from the five previous days of the same kind that did not have a critical event (five last weekdays or five last weekend days) to estimate a regular consumption.

item.title: Winter Credit Sensors
item.description:
Sensor description

The following entities are created for the DCPC (Winter Credits) rate. Peak event entities read their data from the dedicated calendar configured in the integration. For details about each period, see the optimization logic page.

Warning

Entities that represent the current state (Winter Credit Status, Critical Peak Active, Preheat Active) depend on the calendar events and the coordinator update. For automations that must run at a precise time, prefer the timestamp entities (Next Anchor Start, Next Peak Start, Next Preheat Start, etc.).

item.title: Known Issues
item.description:
Consumption does not sync

Occasional issue

During the start or end of the billing period, consumption is not available in the portal, so HydroQC is unable to retrieve it. Wait two or three days after the start of your billing period and consumption should start syncing again on its own.

Long-term history does not sync

When the integration has been running for a while, the consumption history import can stop responding. If you plan to import your long-term historical data, restart Home Assistant before running the import.

item.title: Obtaining your account information
item.description:
The developpers of the project don’t have access to all of the account types and options available at Hydro-Quebec and rely on information provided by the users to implement them.

If your account type is not supported yet it may be helpful for us if you can provide the information available in your Hydro-Quebec customer portal.

Important

Please make sure to remove all your personal information from the outputs before sending it to us.

item.title: Diagnostic tool
item.description:
Diagnostic tool

The Hydroqc library includes a diagnostic tool to recover all the available data from your Hydro-Québec account in a format allowing us to investigate specific problems.

Important

To be used on the express request of developers only

Most problems can be resolved from available logs. Please send us diagnostic data only when asked.

Installation

At first you must install the hydroqc library in a virtual environment Python.
